components.name: Segmented Device Filter
components.description: A compact three-way population filter with one physically lifted active option.
components.css: .ds-segmented { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); padding: 3px; border-radius: 10px; background: #eaf0f4; } .ds-segment { min-height: 34px; padding: 0 7px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; color: #526579; background: transparent; font: 750 11px 'Pretendard Variable', Pretendard, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-segment.active { color: var(--ink); background: white; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(17,40,60,.1); } .ds-segment:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(8,127,140,.28); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Measurement Field
components.description: A monospaced numeric field with an attached unit cell.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 8px; color: #354b60; font: 800 11px 'Pretendard Variable', Pretendard, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-input-unit { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #b9c7d2; border-radius: 9px; background: white; } .ds-input-unit:focus-within { border-color: var(--nmos); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(8,127,140,.1); } .ds-input-unit input { min-width: 0; height: 38px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; outline: 0; color: var(--ink); background: transparent; font: 400 12px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace; } .ds-input-unit > span { padding: 0 10px; display: grid; place-items: center; color: var(--muted); background: #edf2f5; font-size: 10px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a bright, compact engineering instrument rather than a dashboard of detached metric cards. Ink-blue structure anchors a paper-gray workbench; phosphor cyan and magenta make NMOS and PMOS populations legible without turning the screen into decoration.

The system prioritizes scanability, traceability, and defensible decisions. Dense controls remain calm through a tight type ramp, repeated 18px rhythm, continuous chart-and-ledger surfaces, and color that is reserved for device polarity, state, and action.
keyCharacteristics: Bright laboratory workbench with ink-blue instrument structure.
Cyan NMOS and magenta PMOS as a persistent analytic pairing.
Rounded white surfaces with restrained ambient lift.
Monospaced measurement entry and tabular numeric output.

rules.name: The Two-Channel Rule
rules.body: Cyan denotes NMOS or active interaction; magenta denotes PMOS. Do not swap or reuse this pair for unrelated categories.

rules.name: The Ink Structure Rule
rules.body: Ink blue is structural and informational, not a general-purpose filled-card color; use it for app chrome, aggregate status, and transient feedback.

rules.name: The Instrument Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Use only one display statement; everything inside the workbench steps down to title, body, label, or mono roles.

rules.name: The Continuous Evidence Rule
rules.body: Keep summary, plots, and ledger in one reading path; do not fragment them into independent dashboard tiles.

rules.name: The Ambient-Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows clarify surface level and interaction state; they never become decorative hard offsets.

dos: Do preserve the cyan-NMOS and magenta-PMOS mapping across curves, chips, annotations, and filters.
Do keep extraction method, fit state, thresholds, and caveats visible near the analytical evidence.
Do use the repeated 18px rhythm for workbench gaps and primary surface padding.
Do retain strong keyboard focus and the reduced-motion override.
donts: Don't split aggregate evidence into a field of detached metric cards.
Don't use PMOS magenta as a generic accent or action color.
Don't add decorative gradients, hard offset shadows, or ornamental display type to the laboratory workbench.
Don't hide failure, no-fit, method, or source provenance behind color alone.
